_comment: Octail curated egg (plan §6.4). Based on games-steamcmd rising_world/unity/egg-rising-world-unity.json (pelican-eggs, MIT licence), for the current Rising World (the Unity version, the public branch of app 339010; the Java version is the old 'java' branch and not shipped). Octail keeps the Linux server (RisingWorldServer.x64, the executable Steam's launch config names) and the server.properties edits by line (file parser), and adds: the port, max players, seed and Server_ClearConsole=False there too (the server would clear the console window at start), every key Octail sets gets a line when the file has none, the existing server.properties is kept on reinstall, the RCON password is required to be 6 to 64 letters, digits, - and _ (the file says 6 at least) and has no default (upstream: somepassword), RCON gets an automatic port at the game port - 2 (its default 4253 next to 4255), the web/query port the server always opens at the game port - 1 (TCP; the server list and /info use it) is reserved with fixed_ports, the start also counts once the game port is bound (x_octail.features.ready), the rising-world tag, install sandbox defaults and resource hints, the anonymous login only, curl with timeouts and retries, and the install fails when SteamCMD didn't download the server. Rising World's RCON is the game's own tool (RCON_APIOnly, certificates); Octail doesn't connect to it (its protocol couldn't be verified), so console commands go to the server's own input (Server_Input). SteamCMD is retried up to 3 times: its first run on a fresh install often fails with "Missing configuration". SteamCMD exits 0 even when an install failed (Missing configuration), so its retry loop counts a run as done only on SteamCMD's "Success! App" line.
name: Rising World
author: eggs@octail.net
description: Rising World is a voxel-based open-world sandbox: dig, build, farm and survive in a procedurally generated world, alone or with others. The current (Unity) version's Linux dedicated server.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
## Octail curated install: SteamCMD downloads the Linux build of the server.
## Server Files: /mnt/server

## anonymous login: this server needs no Steam account
STEAM_USER=anonymous
STEAM_PASS=""
STEAM_AUTH=""

## download and install steamcmd
cd /tmp || exit 1
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300 --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 -o steamcmd.tar.gz https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz || { echo "Downloading SteamCMD failed."; exit 1; }
tar -xzvf steamcmd.tar.gz -C /mnt/server/steamcmd
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamapps # Fix steamcmd disk write error when this folder is missing
cd /mnt/server/steamcmd || exit 1

# SteamCMD fails otherwise for some reason, even running as root.
# This is changed at the end of the install process anyways.
chown -R root:root /mnt
export HOME=/mnt/server

## install game using steamcmd
## Octail: SteamCMD's first run often fails with "Missing configuration"; try up to 3 times
for steamcmd_try in 1 2 3; do
    if ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /mnt/server +login ${STEAM_USER} ${STEAM_PASS} ${STEAM_AUTH} +app_update ${SRCDS_APPID} $( [[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAID} ]] || printf %s "-beta ${SRCDS_BETAID}" ) $( [[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAPASS} ]] || printf %s "-betapassword ${SRCDS_BETAPASS}" ) validate +quit 2>&1 | tee /tmp/steamcmd.log && grep -q "Success! App '" /tmp/steamcmd.log && ! grep -q "ERROR! Failed to install app" /tmp/steamcmd.log; then break; fi
    echo "SteamCMD did not finish (attempt $steamcmd_try of 3)"
done

## set up 32 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32
cp -v linux32/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so

## set up 64 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
cp -v linux64/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

## Octail: fail the install when SteamCMD didn't download the server
if [[ ! -f "/mnt/server/RisingWorldServer.x64" ]]; then
    echo -e "\nSteamCMD failed to install the Rising World dedicated server; try reinstalling."
    exit 1
fi
chmod +x /mnt/server/RisingWorldServer.x64

## Octail: server.properties is made once from the shipped server.example.properties (an existing one is kept);
## every key Octail sets before each start ("Key=value", the file parser matches "Key=") gets a line of its own
## when the file has none.
CFG=/mnt/server/server.properties
if [[ ! -f "$CFG" ]]; then
    if [[ -f /mnt/server/server.example.properties ]]; then
        cp /mnt/server/server.example.properties "$CFG"
    else
        printf '%s\n' "# Rising World dedicated server settings, written by the Octail install." > "$CFG"
    fi
fi
sed -i 's/\r$//' "$CFG"
for key in Server_Name Server_Password Server_Port Server_ClearConsole Settings_MaxPlayers World_Name World_GameMode World_Seed RCON_Enabled RCON_Port RCON_Password; do
    grep -q "^${key}=" "$CFG" || echo "${key}=" >> "$CFG"
done
## the shipped screen/start scripts are not used in a container
rm -f /mnt/server/linux_screen.sh /mnt/server/linux_startscript.sh

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Server Name
variables.description: The name in the server list.

variables.name: Server Password
variables.description: Optional: players must enter it to join. Empty = no password (no spaces).

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: The most players online at once.

variables.name: World Name
variables.description: The world to load; a new name creates a new world (the old one stays).

variables.name: Game Mode
variables.description: Survival or Creative, for a new world.

variables.name: Seed
variables.description: Optional: the seed of a new world (a number). Empty = random.

variables.name: RCON
variables.description: True: Rising World's own RCON tool listens on the RCON port (set a password first). Octail's console doesn't use it.

variables.name: RCON Password
variables.description: The RCON password: 6 to 64 letters, digits, - and _.

variables.name: RCON Port
variables.description: RCON (TCP). Set by Octail when the server is created (two below the game port).

variables.name: Auto Update
variables.description: Update the server with SteamCMD before every start (1 = on, 0 = off).
